expectations.evidence: The page swaps the ticket-sales claim for a reach claim: "a growing reach asset." It gives non-ticket reasons to keep the channel: reach beyond the room, a durable archive, speaker value and sponsor/partner inventory. It says outright that "none depends on ticket conversion," and the decision it asks for is "Approve continued investment... on its reach and archive value." The relationship side is thinner. expectations.text: Argues reach and relationship value in place of a registration claim
expectations.evidence: The page argues for reach in place of a sales claim. It renames the channel a "reach and ticket-page exposure channel" and refuses the "top of funnel for ticket sales" label until data supports it. It asks the board to "Approve the channel as a reach investment" and to hold the "drives ticket sales" claim. Reach gets real support: 12,000 subscribers as an owned audience with no per-impression cost, and +40% views year over year. Relationship value is only implied.
